international.title: Campaigners urge Albanese government to reject ‘climate bomb’ coalmine expansion after Cop31
international.summary: Hunter Valley Operations expansion in New South Wales would allow additional 430m tonnes of coal to be extracted and burned Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here Climate campaigners are urging the Albanese government to heed a “line in the sand” warning on fossil fuels issued by dozens of countries at a UN climate summit and refuse a massive coalmine expansion planned in New South Wales. A proposed agreement at the Cop31 negotiations in Turkey failed after a list of nations – including European Union members, Panama, the Marshall Islands, Vanuatu, Norway and Belize – said they would not support it unless it included an explicit statement that the world needed to transition away from fossil fuels.
